questions.q: Why does documentation matter more in a financial system than in a typical IT support ticket?
options: The numbers touched feed statements and audits, so the reasoning behind a change needs to be findable later
It doesn't — the standard is the same everywhere
Financial systems never get audited
Only security tickets need documentation
questions.explain: A manual adjustment or data fix in a financial system can be questioned by an auditor later, so the note needs to make the reasoning findable.

questions.q: Which of these is a properly specific root cause statement?
options: "Data issue"
"Fixed it"
"Invoice distribution total was $30 short of the header amount due to a freight line added after distributions were generated"
"User error"
questions.explain: A good root cause names the specific condition found — in this case, an exact dollar mismatch and why it occurred — not a vague category.

questions.q: What does 'verification' mean in a resolution note?
options: Asking the user if they are happy with the response
The specific check performed that proves the fix actually worked, such as re-running a process
A guess about whether the fix probably worked
A signature from a manager
questions.explain: Verification is a concrete, repeatable check — like re-running Validate and confirming the invoice reaches Validated status — not an assumption.

questions.q: A consultant reapplies a misapplied receipt correctly but never confirms why the original misapplication happened. What should the resolution note say?
options: State a confident root cause anyway, since the symptom is fixed
Leave the root cause section blank
Claim the fix prevents any recurrence
State plainly that the underlying cause wasn't fully confirmed and recommend monitoring
questions.explain: The lesson stresses honesty: documenting more confidence than you actually have is worse than plainly stating what wasn't confirmed.

questions.q: In the Meridian Steel Fabricators example note, why is it important that the note explicitly says 'no setup change was required'?
options: Without it, a reader might wrongly assume a tolerance or hold rule was changed, affecting other suppliers
It isn't important and could be left out
It proves the clerk didn't make a mistake
It is required by Oracle's system design
questions.explain: Explicitly stating that no setup changed prevents a future reader from assuming a broader rule (affecting other suppliers or transactions) was modified.
